page: Amazon Web Services m5ad.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz. The instance provisions 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores utilizing simultaneous multithreading, alongside 16 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz. The hardware layout adheres to a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, offering 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Included directly with the host configuration is a bundled 150 GB local NVMe solid-state drive for high-speed ephemeral scratch storage, accompanied by a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. No dedicated graphics accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are attached.

Benchmark measurements reflect the entry-level baseline capabilities of the first-generation AMD EPYC architecture. Compute-focused metrics from stress-ng and Geekbench place both single-threaded (718.0) and multi-threaded (1724.0) throughput within the lower performance brackets. Memory bandwidth tests yield 26.66 GB/sec on uncached large read blocks and 13.97 GB/sec on writes. However, hardware cryptographic extensions including AES and SHA-NI assist in maintaining standard throughput on PassMark CPU encryption evaluations (3242.61). Application-level testing exhibits moderate throughput, registering 2.44 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.07 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m5ad.xlarge provides an economical balance of compute cores, general-purpose memory, and direct-attached NVMe storage without requiring external EBS volume attachments for temporary data. The primary architectural tradeoff centers on raw per-core execution speeds and older instruction support, as modern AVX-512 and matrix extensions are absent. The configuration fits non-latency-critical general-purpose workloads, including continuous integration build agents, batch processing pipelines, caching layers, and development databases requiring fast local I/O.
description: Amazon Web Services m5ad.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System, driven by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz. The instance allocates 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 16 GB of DDR4 memory at a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Local ephemeral storage is provided via a bundled 150 GB NVMe SSD, delivering low-latency access for temporary data, while networking delivers a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark results indicate modest compute and memory throughput, placing single-core and multi-core evaluations in the lower tiers, though hardware cryptographic acceleration scores solidly on PassMark encryption tests. Lacking discrete graphics hardware, the instance represents an entry-tier x86 configuration balancing predictable baseline processing against cost-effective local scratch disk performance. It serves caching layers, build environments, batch processing, and lightweight database workloads requiring fast local disk I/O.
